ideas.title: Three hulls in the bay
ideas.critique: Buoyancy integrated from the hull's own mesh, with a righting moment, is physics the island has never had, and three near-identical hulls that settle three different ways is a payoff a stranger can read at a glance. The risk is that the film turns into one more set of objects moving on their own in front of a fixed camera, the same as the tops, unless the carving and launching actually reach the player.

ideas.title: Hang the lantern on the hook
ideas.nearest: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: The strong part is that the wire is used: a load yields the bends joint by joint, so the hook holds or opens because of how it was bent, and the next try matters. It is still the same wire bench, and a lantern sliding off a hook is a small visual payoff, so if the mouse grip is clumsy it will look like a refinement only.

ideas.title: The stream answers a stone
ideas.nearest: Skipping stones, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Real shallow-water flow on the island's heightfield, with banking, jets and drifting sticks, is new and playable, and the dam-break test against the Ritter solution makes it honest. It does little for the making-things goal, and 10 cm cells over the whole stream on Mantle may be too slow to run live, which would leave only a film.

ideas.title: Lumi falls for real
ideas.critique: Active ragdoll falls with a balance controller that lets go and a get-up routine are exactly what the island's animation lacks, and funny falls get clipped and shared. Getting-up controllers are hard to make look good, and a half-working one will read as jitter and popping, which the motion measure will catch.

ideas.title: The potter's wheel in Jump in
ideas.critique: This is the core of the big goal: the player throws, cuts and fires a jug in one sitting. But the glaze pooling in cuts has been shown already, and the only new physics is a slump check, so a watcher sees the jar post again with a hand on the wheel.

ideas.title: A plank bridge that sags
ideas.nearest: Thin ice, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Friends crossing a plank that creaks and cracks under the heavy one is a readable, funny moment, and cut thickness deciding the outcome ties it to making. Euler-Bernoulli deflection is textbook and the crack is likely scripted at a stress threshold, and friends breaking through has been tried before on the ice.

ideas.title: Paper that flutters down
same_form: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
Dandelion clocks, a take that misses
ideas.critique: A pitching moment that makes real flutter and tumble is a genuine fix to PrintSim, but the island has dropped paper twice already, and three sheets falling side by side is the same falling-object film once more. Folds that stay are the part that matters, and the pitch leaves them for last.

ideas.title: Wet sand holds a wall
ideas.nearest: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Sand whose cohesion follows moisture, drying pale and slumping, is a material with real state and a race against the sun is a game. A column model with an angle-of-repose rule is a cellular-automaton effect rather than granular physics, so close up it may look like a heightmap sinking.

ideas.title: The owl hunts by ear
ideas.critique: A sneaking game in which the ground's material sets how loud each step is gives the existing owl and echo code something to do. In practice it is a loudness threshold with a head turn, the night owl has been posted, and the big goal hardly moves.

ideas.title: A glass bubble someone holds
ideas.critique: Glass blowing has already had a film and a still, and a sagging bubble that cools was the payoff of both. Lumi's beak holding the pipe fixes a flaw people noticed, but a watcher would see the same post again.
